source: Korea Herald — BOK 2026 growth outlook preview
evidence: Given the stronger-than-expected exports led by semiconductors, increased government expenditure driven by higher tax revenues and a rebound in domestic demand, the country is likely to achieve economic growth of around 3 percent this year. — Ahn Jae-kyun, Korea Investment & Securities (analyst consensus previewing a BOK 2026 growth-outlook revision from 2.6% to 3.0-3.4%)

source: Korea Herald — record current account surplus
evidence: S. Koreas current account surplus hit a fresh record in June at $49.73 billion, pushing the H1 2026 cumulative surplus to $191.01 billion — about 4x the $47.87 billion in H1 2025, and already exceeding the BOKs earlier full-half projection of $151.5 billion. — Korea Herald / BOK data, Aug 6 2026

Koreas August exports jumped 68.7% YoY to $98.25 billion on chip demand; semiconductor exports hit a record $46.7 billion (up 209% YoY, 47.5% of total exports), trade surplus near $34.8 billion, second-highest on record. Exports to China +119.3% to $24.1bn, to US +89.3% to $16.5bn. — Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy data via Korea Times, Sep 1 2026

source: Korea Times/CNBC — MSCI market classification review
evidence: MSCI kept South Korea out of its Developed Markets watchlist in the 2026 annual market classification review (announced 23 June 2026), citing the wons limited offshore convertibility, limited operational adoption of omnibus accounts/in-kind transfers, and thin onshore liquidity during extended FX trading hours. Koreas Finance Ministry said reforms were still underway. — Korea Times/CNBC, Jun 24 2026
